text:
Ilya (PM): quick sync: a few enterprise customers asked for higher-dim embeddings (4096, 8192) and the ability to request multiple dims in one API call. need a clear MVP definition by EOD.
Sam (eng-platform): high level: 4096 on hosted seems feasible with text-embedding-3-large. 8192 will likely be Dedicated-only due to GPU memory. multi-dim in a single request complicates batching/caching.
Priya (eng-ml): model note: our current embedding stack optimized for 1536/2048. 4096 requires retrain/tuning of model variants; performance impact expected but acceptable. 8192 is non-trivial 12-we'd need parameter-shard or a new arch.
Noah (devrel): from SDKs perspective: customers want an easy single-call workflow. many will prefer server-side aggregation. However, client-side fanout is simpler to launch.
Jin (CS): customers (legal search, recommendation engines) prioritized single-call for latency determinism. they'd accept enterprise gating for 8192.
Ilya (PM): options: 1) MVP: single-dim per request, support up to 4096 hosted. 2) MVP+: allow multi-dim server-side and return a nested response. 3) Enterprise path: 8192 via Dedicated/private. Thoughts?
Sam (eng-platform): prefer option 1 for predictability. For option 2 we need to change response schema and add validation/size checks. Also adds complexity to autoscaling.
Priya (eng-ml): agree option 1 lowest risk. Option 2 implies we must handle per-dim batching windows separately which will bloat queueing logic.
Noah (devrel): compromise: launch option 1, provide an SDK helper to fan-out and re-aggregate results client-side, plus example code. That meets most needs quickly.
Jin (CS): can we promise p95 latency targets to customers? they want <=250ms for small batches (<=8) at 4096.
Sam (eng-platform): target seems tight but possible with kernel optimizations and restricting batch sizes: max_batch_size 12 for 4096 on hosted. We'll need perf runs.
Priya (eng-ml): perf plan: tune GEMM kernels and test KV cache memory footprint. I'll prepare bench scripts for 1536/2048/4096.
Ilya (PM): API design thoughts: keep existing "data" array for single-dim responses. If we later add multi-dim, require explicit param multi_dim=true and return a versioned field like "data_v2". Avoid breaking existing clients.
Sam (eng-platform): agreed. Also expose model metadata endpoint with max_dim and max_batch_size so SDKs can auto-split. Add an explicit HTTP 431 with reason when request too large.
Noah (devrel): SDK behavior: auto-split by max_batch_size, optional auto-parallelize for multi-dim by issuing parallel requests and merging. We'll supply examples for JS/Python.
Jin (CS): customer comms: I'll preface beta invites: "hosted beta: 4096 available (limited), 8192 on Dedicated contact sales". Keep multi-dim server-side as "coming later".
Ilya (PM): launch criteria:
- Perf: 4096 p95 <= 250ms on small batches <=8 in canary
- SDKs updated with auto-split helper and examples
- Docs: clear section on client-side fanout and data format
- CS: at least 3 enterprise beta customers confirmed
- Canary: 7 days of stable telemetry
Priya (eng-ml): timeline: I can deliver perf harness + quality evals for 4096 in 2 weeks. 8192 research is 6-10 weeks.
Sam (eng-platform): infra tasks: model metadata endpoint, per-model batch caps, mem guardrails per-tenant, routing 8192-only requests to Dedicated. I'll draft an RFC.
Noah (devrel): will draft SDK helpers this sprint. include a toggle to opt into server-side multi-dim when it ships.
Jin (CS): I'll assemble beta list and notify top customers.
Ilya (PM): decision: ship MVP = option 1 (single-dim per request, hosted 4096 beta). Defer server-side multi-dim and 8192 to enterprise roadmap. Draft RFC due Friday.
Sam (eng-platform): noted. I'll add model metadata and the 431 error semantics into the RFC.
Priya (eng-ml): will schedule perf runs.
Noah (devrel): will prepare code snippets for client-side fanout + sample concat/merge logic.
ci-bot: Canary lane available Tuesday 06:00 UTC.
Ilya (PM): thanks team 10-will sync Friday 11am to review RFC and beta customer list.
